title: Devin: The AI Software Engineer
hook: Cognition's Devin was marketed as the first 'AI software engineer' — an autonomous agent that plans, writes, runs, and debugs code across a whole task in its own sandbox.
key_points: Launched March 2024 by Cognition; billed as the first autonomous AI software engineer.
Works in a sandbox with its own shell, code editor, and browser to complete tasks end-to-end.
Takes a natural-language goal, makes a plan, then writes, tests, and fixes the code.
Sparked debate about how far autonomous coding agents can replace engineers.
content_html: Devin, launched by Cognition in March 2024, was presented as the first "AI software engineer" — an agent meant to complete entire development tasks autonomously rather than just suggest code. Given a natural-language goal, Devin draws up a step-by-step plan and then executes it inside a sandboxed environment equipped with its own shell, code editor, and web browser.
extra_html:
What's new

Where most coding assistants of the time autocompleted within an editor, Devin operated as a full agent: it could write code, run it, read the errors, fix them, and iterate until the task was done, browsing documentation along the way. Cognition demonstrated it resolving real issues and emphasized end-to-end autonomy. Later versions (Devin 2.0) dropped the price dramatically and improved task completion.

Why it matters

Devin crystallized the "autonomous coding agent" category and the debate around it — both excitement about agents that own a task and skepticism after developers stress-tested its real-world reliability. Measured against benchmarks like SWE-bench, it helped set expectations (and controversy) for what agentic coding could actually deliver, and it pushed the whole field toward agent-first developer tools.

related.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
related.hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.

related.title: Codex: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
related.hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.

related.title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
related.hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

choices.text: It acted as a full agent — writing, running, reading errors, and iterating end-to-end
It autocompleted code inline within an editor
It only generated single functions from docstrings

flashcards.prompt: What tools does Devin operate with inside its sandbox?
flashcards.back_html: Its own shell, code editor, and web browser, which it uses to complete development tasks end-to-end.
